newsitem.title: USA: 3M sees CFC replacement product sales rising.
newsitem.headline: 3M sees CFC replacement product sales rising.

text.p: Minnesota Mining and Manufacturing said Wednesday annual sales of its CFC replacement products would reach $400 million by the year 2000.

"We estimate sales of our perfluorocarbons and our hydrofluoroether will reach $400 million in 2000, from $100 million in 1995," said Jay Ihlenfeld, business director in the company's specialty chemicals division.
The products replace chlorofluorocarbons, which were banned under the Montreal Protocol, which was approved by 150 countries, including the United States, in 1987.
Ihlenfeld said Minnesota Mining would triple its chemical production capacity, with half of that being devoted to the replacement products.
"We plan to triple our specialized chemical productioin capacity by 2000, with half of that devoted to PFC anbd HFE proeduction," he told analysts at a meeting here.
